analysis: Examined the provider-swift ProviderCore changes. (1) ProviderLoop+ModelSwitch.swift line 46 adds transitionGenerations.begin(.modelSwitch) just before modelSwitchTask is set. Ownership and drain checks (lines 24-37, 146-151) are unchanged. The visible code gives no sign of a security regression, but I could not see how transitionGenerations is consumed (for example by App Attest or serving-authorization generations under T-053/TB-011), so that is a question for integration. (2) ProviderLoop+Prefetch.swift lines 46-57 reroute prefetch_model requests for builds outside ordinarily selected serving. This applies when autopilotConsented is set and the model is not in ordinaryServingModelIDs. If autopilot downloads are enabled, the request goes to handleAutopilotDownloadRequest. Otherwise it fails with model_not_selected. This narrows the ordinary path, since a coordinator-sent prefetch can no longer reach ordinary serving without prior membership. It is a restriction, not a new exposure. The remaining checks (runtime eligibility, shutdown, draining) are skipped on the autopilot branch, so they must be enforced inside handleAutopilotDownloadRequest. That function is not in the supplied evidence. Line 353 swaps autopilotSettings.allows for autopilotSetAllows, whose definition is not visible. (3) ProviderLoop+PrefetchPublication.swift: selfTestRecordRefuses is now internal (line 25). beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence(modelId) is called at line 48 before the publication counter increments. At lines 261-265, a verified build is added to autopilotInventoryModels when joinsAutopilotSetWhenVerified(info) holds. This follows the hash-verified publication path, but I could not check that the helper requires consent, runtime eligibility and a non-failed self-test, or that the advertised models_update stays gated by coordinator-side authorization (TB-002, T-027). Remaining integration questions: the definitions of handleAutopilotDownloadRequest, autopilotSetAllows and joinsAutopilotSetWhenVerified, the consumers of transitionGenerations, and the behavior of beginModelAdvertisementOccurrence. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
